title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 33-35): Grothendieck is proving an injectivity statement, the map (16)/(*)/(**), needed for an anabelian rigidity result ('th. 3', 'cor. 1 b)'): two maps f, g from X to a curve Y that induce the same map on fundamental groups should be equal. The reduction is to the generalized Jacobian G = G_Y, a semi-abelian variety over a finitely generated field K. The claim is that the Kummer-type map G(K) -> lim_n H^1(K, nG) = H^1(K, T(G)) is injective. On the previous page the kernel is identified with the infinitely divisible elements, the intersection over n of nG(K). By Mordell-Weil/Lang-Neron, G(K) is finitely generated, so this intersection is 0. A remark adds that all primes l must be used: with only one l, or away from p, a point of order p gives a counterexample.

This page restates the result geometrically. A point x in G(K) defines a torsor under T_infinity(G) = lim nG. That torsor is the fibre over x of the 'universal abelian covering' G~ = lim (G <-n- G), the projective system of the self-covers G(n) = G given by multiplication by n. The theorem says: if x is 'trivial', i.e. x lifts to K-points at every level n, then x = 0.

This remains true in characteristic p > 0, but there the isogenies n_G with p | n are not etale, so the statement is no longer about fundamental groups. One fix is to replace p_G by its quotient by its radicial part. Equivalently, work in a category of 'quasi-varietes' in which finite radicial surjective morphisms (universal homeomorphisms) are made invertible. Either way one works only with the prime-to-p part of H_1(G-bar). In that setting the statement says that the existence of liftings, up to radicial morphisms over K, forces x = 0. A priori x is then only p-torsion.

Grothendieck judges this form of th. 3 in char p useless ('fait une belle jambe'). To be comfortable one must prove it with prime-to-p fundamental groups. But already for an elliptic curve Y, for suitable base fields where rational p-torsion points exist, the injectivity of (**) is false. Indeed, for a finitely generated abelian group A, the intersection of nA over n prime to p is exactly the p-primary torsion of A.

The next page continues: injectivity of (*) might still hold without characteristic hypothesis. For cor. 1 b) in char p with prime-to-p groups, one gets that g(x) - f(x) is p-power torsion in G_Y, so f = g when G is a torus (genus-0 case), since tori have no nontrivial p-torsion rational points. In general one gets a compatible system: Q' - P' is p-torsion in G_{Y'} for all prime-to-p Galois covers Y'. He is unsure whether this forces P = Q.
errors: No mathematical error. The observation that prime-to-p injectivity fails is correct: the kernel of G(K) -> H^1(K, T^{(p')}G) is the p-primary torsion of the finitely generated group G(K), which can be nonzero (e.g. ordinary elliptic curves with a rational p-torsion point).

The phrase 'C'est vrai en car. p>0 ...' in the transcription likely reads 'également' (also true in char p) rather than 'évidemment'. The claim is correct either way, given the Lang-Neron finiteness used on the previous page.

ideas.what: Reformulating Kummer-map injectivity as: a rational point lifting to every level of the 'universal abelian covering' lim(G <-n- G) must be 0
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map G(K) -> H^1(K, TG) injectivity; adelic/profinite Tate module torsors
ideas.where_published: Related remarks appear in the letter to Faltings (1983) and the Esquisse

ideas.what: In char p, work in a category where finite radicial surjective morphisms are inverted ('quasi-variétés'), so that p-isogenies become harmless
ideas.modern_name: Localization at universal homeomorphisms / perfection of schemes; topological invariance of the etale site
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 1 IX, SGA 4 VIII) for invariance; later perfect schemes (Bhatt-Scholze) and Kollár on universal homeomorphisms
ideas.where_published: Etale invariance under universal homeomorphisms is in SGA 1/SGA 4; the 'quasi-variétés' category as such is unsure

ideas.what: Recognition that the anabelian rigidity/section-type statements in char p with prime-to-p fundamental groups only determine points up to p-power torsion (Frobenius/radicial ambiguity), and that the naive injectivity fails
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian geometry in positive characteristic; section conjecture up to Frobenius twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Stix (2002, curves over function fields of char p, with Frobenius twists); Tamagawa; Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Not in the published Esquisse in this detail as far as known

missed.claim: Grothendieck already in c. 1981 isolates the characteristic-p obstruction to anabelian rigidity. Prime-to-p Kummer maps for generalized Jacobians have p-primary torsion kernel, so maps or points are determined only up to p-torsion / radicial (Frobenius) ambiguity. He proposes inverting finite radicial surjective morphisms as the right framework, and asks (next page) whether a compatible system of p-torsion differences over all prime-to-p covers forces P = Q.
missed.quote: travaillant dans la cat. des "quasi-variétés" où on rend inversibles les morphismes finis radiciels surjectifs ... l'injectivité de (**) est fausse
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the 'up to Frobenius twist' formulations of positive-characteristic anabelian results (Stix and others). It is mainly of historical interest, since the phenomenon has since been rediscovered and treated. The specific question on the next page, about the tower of prime-to-p covers killing p-torsion ambiguity, could be checked against the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful early unpublished diagnosis of the characteristic-p issue in anabelian rigidity, with the idea of localizing at radicial morphisms. Later literature treats this through Frobenius twists, so it is a historical precedent rather than a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'les G ne sont pas stables' should read 'les n_G (or p_G) ne sont pas étales'.
'C'est vrai en car. p>0 évidemment' probably reads 'C'est vrai en car. p>0 également'.
'avec la partie première[?] des H_1' should read 'avec la partie première à p des H_1(Ḡ)'.
'la validité ... en de la car. nulle fait une belle jambe' is more likely 'la validité sous cette forme du th. 3 en car. p>0 nous fait une belle jambe'.
'(Un et voudrait on a dans VA...' is uncertain; it plausibly reads 'Bien sûr x est de p-torsion' followed by a remark about px = 0.
